correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 the sunlet graph is explicitly specified by a simple adjacency formula on C_n times {0,1}. A full FO-type recurrence (atomic equality/adjacency diagram and the SET of all one-point extension types) is proved complete by induction for quantifier rank r. Two independent implementations were run from the actual package paths: full ordered-tuple enumeration through n=12 and dihedral-orbit reduction through n=15, both producing precisely the classes {3},{4},{5},{6},{7},{8},{9},{>=10} over their checked ranges, with exact common stage counts 116,122,46,14,8. The dihedral canon normalization is proved an automorphism orbit representative even with repeated selections. Brown–Hoshino Theorem 4.9 proves C_n equivalent at rank four for n>=11, and the explicit side-preserving coordinate-game lift to C_n corona K1 is a valid partial-isomorphism strategy, establishing all n>=11. The finite n=10~n=11 bridge proves the infinite final class by transitivity; all seven smaller representatives are separated by exact complete finite types. The 20-vertex bound is sharp within the stated family. No finite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The closest fully inspected logic theorem is Brown and Hoshino, 2007, Theorem 4.9, which classifies plain cycles and implies only the sunlet upper cutoff n>=11 via game transfer; it does not imply the key equivalence n=10 and n=11 or the precise smaller classes. Accessible work treating sunlets focuses on connected safe numbers and general corona spectra, not bounded-rank logical classification. Archive deduplication and indexed searches for sunlet, sun graph, hairy cycle, corona of a cycle, quantifier rank and Ehrenfeucht–Fraisse gave no prior statement that covers all eight classes. This is a qualified best-knowledge judgment, not certified historical priority.
residual_risks: The 2007 corona-spectrum source was not inspected in complete full text, although its published abstract describes unrelated spectral theorems.

value.rationale: A complete natural classification of all finite connected unicyclic graphs obtained by attaching one leaf at every vertex of a cycle is structurally meaningful in bounded-depth model theory. Its sharp length-10 threshold and 20-vertex representative are not covered by the plain-cycle threshold 11: the pendant corona changes exactly where four-round logic stabilizes. The result is a reusable exact example for first-order preservation under graph corona construction, with two independent finite checkers and a separate infinite mathematical argument. No broader theoretical breakthrough is claimed, and significance is the precise natural classification rather than the mere existence of code.
